VectorStore.updateSparse loses a whole 64-point slice when Qdrant rejects the batch for one unknown id. Bisecting the failing slice would salvage the 63 good points and name the bad id, instead of reporting a round number of losses
auditVectorCoverage reconciles at ENTRY granularity (vectors.allEntryIds() is a set of entry ids), so an entry whose chunks are only partly present in Qdrant reads as covered and gets adopted rather than repaired. Found via entry 7707 on 2026-07-29: one of its 5 chunk points was missing, which made every sparse-rebuild batch containing it fail, and the boot audit then re-marked it as covered. Reconciling per point id would catch it
SEVERE — a 2-second probe can replace the whole index with an inferior one. autoSelect calls ollamaAvailable(), a single fetch with AbortSignal.timeout(2000) and no retry; on a loaded host that times out easily. The chain: probe fails -> bundled 384-dim provider -> collection name encodes the dim, so a NEW empty collection -> backfill re-embeds all 326k entries on the CPU model -> active_collection is published, switching search to the inferior index -> reclaimOrphans then DROPS the good 768 collection. Observed live on 2026-07-29 during a make restart-build while the host was at load 26: the indexer booted on bundled/384 and started building the new collection. Caught only by reading the boot log; nothing alerts, and the 'publish only after the backfill completes' guard bought hours but would not have prevented the switch. Fix candidates: retry the probe (3x with backoff) before conceding; refuse to switch collections when the catalog already has a fully-populated one under a different embedder unless explicitly allowed (an EMBEDDINGS_PROVIDER=auto downgrade is never what an operator meant); and surface 'running on a fallback embedder' on /api/dashboard health rather than only in docker logs
